q: What are the emissions from thermoplastic road marking?
title: Thermoplastic road marking: emissions
short: Thermoplastic paint is melted in kettles, usually fired by LPG, then laid hot. The LPG is Scope 1 for the marking contractor. The paint itself, resin, glass beads and pigment, is Scope 3. Record LPG and kilograms of paint per km of marking.
audience: Road marking contractors and highway agencies

ul: Kilograms of thermoplastic and glass beads laid.

p: Marking is small next to bitumen and aggregates, but it recurs every few years, so it adds up over a road's life.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard
